Inglewood, California
  March 15, 2022

The City Council of the City of Inglewood, California held a regular meeting on Tuesday
March 15, 2022, in the Council Chambers in City Hall of said City.

Mayor Butts called the City Council into Closed Session at the hour of 1:00 p.m.

The Acting City Clerk announced the presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:  Mayor Butts, Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, and
  Faulk; and
  Absent:  None.

City officials and personnel present for closed session were as follows:

  Angela Allen  Acting City Clerk
  Artie Fields  City Manager
  Ken Campos  City Attorney

PUBLIC COMMENTS REGARDING CLOSED SESSION ITEMS. Mayor Butts
inquired if there were any persons present who wished to address the City Council on the
Closed Session Items.

There was no response.

Mayor Butts recessed the City Council at the hour of 1:01 p.m. for Closed Session Item
Nos. CS-1, and CS-2.

  ******************************

Following the Pledge of Allegiance to the flag of our Country, Mayor Butts called the
City Council into joint session with the Successor Agency, and Housing Authority at the
hour of 2:01 p.m.
The City Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary announced the
presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:  Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman
  Butts, Council Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing
  Authority Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, and Faulk; and
  Absent:  None.
City/Successor Agency/Housing Authority officials and personnel present were as
follows:
  Aisha L. Thompson  City Clerk/Secretary*
  Artie Fields  City Manager/Executive Director*
  Ken Campos  City Attorney/General Counsel*
  Louis Atwell  Assistant City Manager/Public Works Director
  Angela Allen  Deputy City Clerk

* Serves as indicated for the Successor Agency and Housing Authority.
PUBLIC COMMENTS – AGENDA ITEMS. Mayor/Successor Agency
Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman Butts inquired if there were any persons present
who wished to address the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority on any
item on the Agendas, other than the public hearings.
   March 15, 2022

  Nancy Hanna, Better Neighbors of Los Angeles, commented on Agenda Item No. PH-2,
  A public hearing to consider the extension of urgency interim Ordinance No. 22-05. She
  spoke in favor of the proposal and applauded the City’s research on the best enforcement
  practices. She also suggested that the City of Inglewood adopt Santa Monica’s standards
  which require all short term rentals to be hosted. Finally, she stated that hosted short term
  rentals protect housing, ensure supervision, reduce nuisance, and safety concerns are
  more effectively and efficiently enforced.

142.9  PAYMENT OF WARRANTS AND BILLS. It was moved by Council Member/
  Successor Agency Member / Housing Authority Member Morales, and seconded by
  Council Member/Successor Agency Member/Housing Authority Member Faulk that the
  demands presented to the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority dated
  March 11, 2022, in the amount of 2,993,322.93 are hereby allowed, and the City
  Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary is hereby authorized to
  certify upon said registers that said demands are so approved. The motion was carried by
  the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing Authority Members
  Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor/Successor Agency
  Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman Butts; and
  Noes: None.

131.9  PUBLIC HEARING HELD - ORDINANCE NO. 22-05A INTRODUCED AND
  ADOPTED - EXTENSION OF URGENCY INTERIM ORDINANCE 22-05 FOR
  AN ADDITIONAL 10 MONTHS AND 15 DAYS OR UPON THE EFFECTIVE
  DATE OF A SHORT TERM RENTAL ORDINANCE. The City Clerk announced
  the next scheduled matter was a public hearing to consider extension of urgency interim
  Ordinance No. 22-05 for an additional 10 months and 15 days or upon the effective date
  of a short term rental ordinance, whichever is first, continuing a moratorium on any and
  all building permits, business licenses, conditional use permits, or any entitlements for
  establishing or expanding any short term rental anywhere in the City of Inglewood, notice
  had been given in the time, form, and manner as required by law, an affidavit was on file,
  and no communications were received.

  Artie Fields, City Manager presented the staff report dated March 15, 2022.

  Alicia Fong, Housing Protection Coordinator presented a brief oral report.

  Mayor Butts inquired if there were any persons present that wished to address the City
  Council on this matter.

  There was no response.

  Furthermore, it was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council
  Member Padilla that Ordinance No. 22-05A entitled:

  EXTENSION OF URGENCY INTERIM ORDINANCE NO. 22-05 FOR
  AN ADDITIONAL TEN MONTHS AND FIFTEEN DAYS OR UPON
  THE EFFECTIVE DATE OF A SHORT TERM RENTAL
  ORDINANCE, WHICHEVER IS FIRST, CONTINUING A
  MORATORIUM ON ANY AND ALL BUILDING PERMITS,
  BUSINESS LICENSES, CONDITIONAL USE PERMITS, OR ANY
  ENTITLEMENTS FOR ESTABLISHING OR EXPANDING ANY
  SHORT TERM RENTAL ANYWHERE IN THE CITY OF
  INGLEWOOD

  was introduced and adopted at the meeting held on March 15, 2022. The motion was
  carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  2
   March 15, 2022

126  PUBLIC HEARING HELD – RECEIVE, CONSIDER, AND DISCUSS THE
  ADJUSTED CENSUS DATA FROM THE NATIONAL DEMOGRAPHICS
  CORPORATION. The City Clerk announced the next scheduled matter was a public
  hearing to receive, consider, and discuss the Adjusted Census Data from the National
  Demographics Corporation, notice had been given in the time, form, and manner as
  required by law, an affidavit was on file, and no communications were received.

  Artie Fields, City Manager, presented the staff report dated March 15, 2022.

  Aisha L. Thompson, City Clerk, gave a brief overview and introduced the presenter.

  Douglass Johnson, National Demographics Corporation (NDC) President, presented a
  slideshow presentation of the draft maps received from the public and those generated by
  NDC. He explained the Federal Rules and State Requirements on how district lines were
  drawn and Rule and Goals of Redistricting. He presented Maps A – D and gave a brief
  narrative regarding each map. Map A: District 3 extends east to Prairie north of
  Manchester, and District 2 picks up Edward Vincent Jr. Park and homes to the north of
  the park. Map B: District 3 extends east to Prairie north of Manchester, but no other
  changes. Map C: District 3 picks up the eastern corner of District 4 and, from District 1,
  the east side of La Brea Ave.; District 2 adds three city blocks from northern District 1;
  District 4 picks up a strip of land from District 1 on the east side of the stadium. Map D:
  District 3 extends east to Prairie north of Manchester; District 2 picks up the west end of
  Edward Vincent Jr. Park. Finally, he stated that all submitted maps met statutory
  requirements.

  Mayor Butts inquired if there were any persons present that wished to address the City
  Council.

  Speaker (Name Unknown) stated that for the City to comply with the FAIR MAPS Act,
  there should have been two public hearings where the public could comment on the
  redistricting of the maps. She also stated this was the first public hearing that the
  community could watch and comment on. The speaker further stated that she sent a cure
  and correct letter to the legislative body regarding the redistricting schedule presented to
  the community. Finally, she recommended Map C because it was the only one that
  divided each district into 25% equal representation.

  Mayor Butts closed the public comments portion at the hour of 2:26 p.m.

  It was moved by Mayor Butts, and seconded by Council Member Morales that the City
  Council does hereby: 1) Receive, consider, and discuss the Adjusted Census Data; 2)
  Consider and discuss Amended draft maps of City Council district boundaries; and 3)
  Receive and file public comments. The motion was carried by the following roll call
  vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  Following discussion, it was moved by Mayor Butts, and seconded by Council Member
  Morales that the City Council does hereby choose Map D as its preferred draft map. The
  motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

132  CLAIMS DENIED. Letters from the Office of the City Attorney recommending the
  following:
  A. Reject Claims Pursuant to Government Code Section 913:
  1. Carl Borack for alleged personal injury; dangerous condition on September 12, 2021.
  2. Lazaro Cabrera for alleged vehicle damage; unidentified stray bullets on January 2,
  2022.
  3. Crystal Calderon for alleged personal injury; dangerous condition on August 28,
  2021.
  4. Maria E. Gonsalez for alleged personal injury; dangerous condition on August 28,
  2021.

  3
   March 15, 2022

  It was moved by Council Member Dotson, and seconded by Council Member Padilla that
  the City Council does hereby Reject Claims listed as A-1 through A-4. The motion was
  carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

156  PAYMENT AUTHORIZED – BIG TIME AFFAIRS LLC. Staff report dated March
  15, 2022, was presented recommending authorization of payment of Invoice No. INV-
  2640 submitted by Big Time Affairs LLC, for use of audio/video (AV) equipment.

  It was moved by Council Member Dotson, and seconded by Council Member Padilla that
  the City Council does hereby authorize payment in the amount of $18,000. The motion
  was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

178  PAYMENT AUTHORIZED – EMERGENCY MANAGEMENT SAFETY
  PARTNERS, LLC. Staff report dated March 15, 2022, was presented recommending
  authorization of payment of Invoice No. 138 submitted by Emergency Management
  Safety Partners, LLC, for planning services related to Super Bowl LVI.

  It was moved by Council Member Dotson, and seconded by Council Member Padilla that
  the City Council does hereby authorize payment in the amount of $13,500. The motion
  was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

178  STATE CITIZENS OPTION FOR PUBLIC SAFETY (COPS OPTION)) GRANT
  FUNDS ACCEPTED; RESOLUTION NO. 22-60 ADOPTED – AMENDING THE
  FISCAL YEAR 2021-2022 BUDGET. Staff report dated March 15, 2022, was
  presented recommending acceptance of the State Citizens Option for Public Safety
  (COPS Option) grant funds in the amount of $168,759.

  It was moved by Council Member Dotson, and seconded by Council Member Padilla that
  the City Council does hereby: 1) Accept funds; 2) Approve the expenditure
  recommendations of the Chief of Police; 3) Authorize inclusion of remaining COPS
  Option grant funds from the previous fiscal year in the amount of $473,865; and 4) Adopt
  Resolution No. 22-60 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA TO AMEND THE FISCAL YEAR
  2021 – 2022 BUDGET TO INCLUDE STATE CITIZEN OPTION
  FOR PUBLIC SAFETY (COPS OPTION) GRANT FUNDS

  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and

183  AMENDMENT NO. 1 TO AGREEMENT NO. 21-010 APPROVED – GANNETT
  FLEMING, INC. Staff report dated March 15, 2022, was presented recommending

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Faulk that

  Noes: None.

  4
   March 15, 2022

  TECHNICAL SERVICES, INC. Staff report dated March 15, 2022, was presented
  recommending approval of Amendment No. 1 to Agreement No. 22-117 with AECOM

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Padilla

132.6  CLOSED SESSION – ANTICIPATED LITIGATION – WORKERS’

  5

126  REPORTS – CITY CLERK. City Clerk Aisha L. Thompson acknowledged her staff for
  their diligent work during the redistricting process. She thanked Elsa Moreno, GIS

  redistricting process. The City Clerk also reminded residents of the redistricting public
  hearing scheduled for March 22, 2022. Finally, she wished everyone a Happy Saint
  Patrick’s Day.

  PUBLIC REMARKS. Mayor Butts inquired if there were any persons present who
  wished to address the City Council on any matter connected with City business not
  elsewhere considered on the Agenda.

  Speaker (Name Unknown), African Town Coalition, spoke regarding residents needing
  rental assistance. He stated that people are still having difficulties getting the necessary
  help. The speaker also mentioned several assistance programs available, and he was
  unsure why people were still struggling. Finally, he thanked the City for hosting the Taste

  Speaker (Name Unknown) commented on Agenda Item Nos. DR-4, Adoption of a

  most equitable in terms of population.

  Michael (Last Name Unknown), Co-Founder of Rainbow Children’s Academy, requested
  assistance with helping to keep his school open because it assisted low-income, single-
  mother, and single-father families in the community.

  Speaker (Name Unknown) spoke concerning the rental assistance program and
  questioned when the funds would be disbursed. She also spoke regarding the closure of

  Speaker (Name Unknown) commented on Agenda Item No. PH-2, Extension of urgency

  effective date of a short-term rental ordinance. He disagreed with the extension of
